mcqs.question: Which of the following reactions is a double displacement (metathesis) reaction?
mcqs.explanation: In a double displacement reaction, the cations and anions of two compounds exchange partners. Option B shows Ag⁺ swapping with Na⁺ to form AgCl and NaNO3, which is a classic double displacement reaction. Option A is a single displacement (metal replaces another metal), C is a combination reaction, and D is a decomposition reaction.

mcqs.question: When aqueous solutions of lead nitrate and potassium iodide are mixed, a yellow precipitate forms. Which compound precipitates out?
mcqs.explanation: Pb(NO3)2 + 2KI → PbI2 + 2KNO3. Lead iodide (PbI2) is insoluble in water and appears as a yellow precipitate. AgCl, BaSO4, and CaCO3 are not formed in this reaction.

mcqs.question: Identify the reaction that represents a displacement (single replacement) reaction.
mcqs.explanation: In a single displacement reaction, a more reactive metal (Zn) displaces a less reactive metal (Cu) from its compound. Option A follows this pattern. Option B is a combination reaction, C is decomposition, and D is a double displacement reaction.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly reflects the relative reactivity of metals in displacement reactions?

options.A: A metal higher in the reactivity series can displace a metal lower in the series from its compound solution.
options.B: A metal lower in the series can displace a metal higher in the series from its compound solution.
options.C: Reactivity does not affect displacement reactions.
options.D: All metals react equally in displacement reactions.

mcqs.answer: A metal higher in the reactivity series can displace a metal lower in the series from its compound solution.
mcqs.explanation: The reactivity series orders metals by their tendency to lose electrons. A more reactive metal can replace a less reactive metal from its salt solution, which is the basis of single displacement reactions. Options B, C, and D contradict this fundamental principle.

mcqs.learning_point: Use metal reactivity to predict displacement
mcqs.question: Given the reactivity series Zn > Fe > Cu, which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Zinc metal will displace iron from FeSO4 solution.
options.B: Iron will displace copper from CuSO4 solution.
options.C: Copper will displace zinc from ZnSO4 solution.
options.D: Iron will displace zinc from ZnSO4 solution.

mcqs.answer: Iron will displace copper from CuSO4 solution.
mcqs.explanation: Because iron is higher than copper in the reactivity series, Fe can replace Cu²⁺ ions in CuSO4, forming FeSO4 and depositing copper metal. Zinc cannot displace iron (A) because Zn is higher, not lower. Copper cannot displace zinc (C), and iron cannot displace zinc (D).

mcqs.question: A student mixes aqueous solutions of Na2CO3 and CaCl2. Which type of reaction occurs?

options.A: Double displacement reaction forming CaCO3 precipitate.

mcqs.answer: Double displacement reaction forming CaCO3 precipitate.
mcqs.explanation: Na2CO3 + CaCl2 → 2NaCl + CaCO3. The carbonate and calcium ions exchange partners, producing insoluble calcium carbonate as a white precipitate—characteristic of a double displacement (metathesis) reaction. The other options do not describe the observed process.

mcqs.question: When aqueous solutions of barium chloride and sodium sulfate are mixed, a white precipitate forms. Which compound is the precipitate?
mcqs.explanation: BaCl2 + Na2SO4 → BaSO4↓ + 2NaCl. Barium sulfate (BaSO4) is insoluble in water and appears as a white precipitate. Sodium chloride remains dissolved, and the other listed compounds are reactants, not products.

mcqs.question: A strip of magnesium metal is placed in a solution of copper(II) sulfate. Which observation best describes the reaction?

options.A: Magnesium dissolves and copper metal deposits on the strip.
options.C: Copper dissolves and magnesium metal deposits.
options.D: Both metals precipitate as insoluble salts.

mcqs.answer: Magnesium dissolves and copper metal deposits on the strip.
mcqs.explanation: Mg is more reactive than Cu, so Mg displaces Cu²⁺ from CuSO4: Mg + CuSO4 → MgSO4 + Cu(s). The magnesium metal goes into solution as Mg²⁺, and copper metal plates out. Options B, C, and D do not follow the reactivity series or the chemistry of the system.
